title: Television credits, including teaching Lift Every Voice and Sing for Bill Cosby
summary: Short notes on the Lena Horne, Carol Burnett, Jack Paar and Mr. Broadway shows, and a vocal group that did not know the Negro national anthem.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Uh-huh. And you did the Lena Horne
special and the Carol Burnett show for Mel Torme and Carol Burnett.
Then this says, on your resume, arranging partial television, Jack Paar Show.
Oh, these were different guests that would come on. It's the same -- practically the same pattern on all the other shows, you know.
Yes, I took over one chapter for Oliver Nelson, you know, because Oliver had to do something else, and I was called in to do this one particular chapter.

Let's see, what did I do on the Bill Cosby special? Oh, yes. That goes back awhile. That was a group of singers. This was vocal writing. And I forget the name of the group now. They were on capital records and they did some work on the Cosby show, you know. I tell you what was so ironic about that. Cosby wanted one particular thing. Cosby wanted the Negro national anthem, "Lift Every Voice and Sing," you know?
And these youngsters never heard of it.
And that was funny, you know? And I said,
"Gee, when I was young I couldn't walk into the house and speak to my father unless I could sing it," you know?

In my day. But these kids don't know anything about that, you know. But I taught it to them, you know. And they could sing. It was a beautiful group, and they did a good job on it. That's about the extent on that, I think.
